config.title: Build OTP input with auto focus behavior

intro.title: Build OTP input with auto focus behavior
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a one-time password (OTP) input component that automatically moves focus to the next field as the user types. You will learn how to manage multiple input elements using state and handle user input with event listeners. The main technologies involved are JavaScript, HTML input elements, and the DOM API for focus control. This project will help you understand dynamic UI updates and user interaction patterns in web development.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for secure authentication flows in real-world applications, such as verifying a user's identity during login, sign-up, or two-factor authentication (2FA). You'll see it in OTP inputs on platforms like banking apps, email verification forms, and password reset screens, where auto-focus improves usability by guiding the user through each digit seamlessly. As a developer, implementing this ensures a smooth, professional user experience that reduces input errors and enhances security in form handling.

objectives: Construct a multi-digit OTP input component with individual input fields
Initialize and manage state to store and update OTP values
Implement auto-focus behavior that moves focus between input fields
Configure event handlers to capture and validate user input
Manipulate DOM references to control focus programmatically
Integrate input validation to ensure only numeric values are accepted
Render a complete OTP interface with proper visual feedback

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Configure input attributes and wire event handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the map callback, configure each input element with type='text', maxLength=1, value={otp[index]}, onChange={(e) => handleChange(index, e.target.value)}, and onKeyDown={(e) => handleKeyDown(index, e)}.
steps.hint: Add these attributes directly to the input element you're returning from the map callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each input element will have the proper attributes and be wired to the handler functions, enabling user interaction.
successCriteria: All input elements have type='text', maxLength=1, value bound to otp state, and onChange/onKeyDown handlers that pass the index and event data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Implement auto-focus logic in handleChange
